title: Will EUR/USD hit __ in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the Investing.com high price (“H”) for any EUR/USD hourly candle for an hour on or before the listed end date (ET) is equal to or above the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Data for a given candle will be considered finalized once the next candle appears on the specified graph. The last trading day of a given week will be considered finalized once the market closes on that day, typically at 5 PM ET on Friday.

This market will resolve as soon as any finalized EUR/USD hourly candle is equal to or above the listed price, or once the final hourly candle in the specified period is finalized. A candle starting at 11:00 PM ET on a given date will be considered to be on that date.

This market’s resolution will be based solely on information from the “H” figure located at the top of the EUR/USD Streaming Chart on Investing.com for the specified currency pair (e.g., https://www.investing.com/currencies/eur-usd-chart).

eventMetadata.context_description:
**EUR/USD has traded near 1.168–1.169 as of August 21, 2026, after rising from the low-1.15 area earlier in the month amid shifting policy expectations and data.**

The primary driver remains the interest-rate differential between the Federal Reserve and European Central Bank. The Fed’s target range sits at 3.50–3.75 percent after holding steady through multiple meetings, with three FOMC members dissenting in favor of a hike at the July gathering. By contrast, the ECB raised its deposit rate to 2.25 percent in June and kept it unchanged in July while signaling openness to further tightening. Market pricing reflects the potential for additional ECB hikes (possibly one more in September) versus a more cautious or on-hold Fed path, narrowing the spread that has long supported the dollar.

Elevated energy prices stemming from Middle East geopolitical tensions have pushed euro-area headline inflation to 2.9 percent in July, with core at 2.5 percent, complicating the ECB’s reaction function and supporting a modestly hawkish tilt. U.S. inflation remains above the Fed’s 2 percent target but has shown some signs of easing in recent prints, while resilient growth and labor-market data keep the door open for further tightening. Euro-area growth has improved modestly but remains fragile, with upcoming flash PMIs, inflation releases, and FOMC minutes likely to influence near-term positioning.

Traders also watch Treasury yields, the dollar’s broader trade-weighted index, and any signals from the Jackson Hole symposium later in August. These factors collectively shape the market-implied path for EUR/USD through the remainder of 2026, with the rate differential and energy-driven inflation serving as the dominant variables.
